candidate.title: CirSeq
candidate.scope: The single RNA-virus CirSeq architecture depicted in the assigned Illumina schematic, interpreted using the supplied Acevedo et al. population-sequencing paper and Acevedo/Andino protocol. One serial route connects whole-genome RNA, short RNA fragments, RNA circles, random-primed tandem-repeat cDNA, aligned repeat observations and a corrected fragment sequence. Broad DNA-library preparation and sequencing records resolve the compressed material-to-data interface using the primary papers. The depicted readout supports genetic-variant analysis within represented viral RNA populations.

states.label: Whole-genome RNA
features: Biological input is viral genomic RNA; the source protocol describes purified viral RNA.
The leftmost example is a yellow-outlined purple strand with a terminal AA(A)n label, depicting a poly(A)-bearing RNA example. The yellow outline has no specified chemical identity.
Poly(A) enrichment or addition is not depicted as an operation.

Overview of the procedure [b00009], RNA fragmentation and size-selection interface
evidence.quote: In Steps 1–18, purified viral RNA is chemically fragmented by Zn2+ to produce RNA in a low-molecular-weight range. states.label: Short linear RNA fragments

Fragment lengths are limited relative to read length so approximately three template copies can fit within one sequencing read; the depicted three-repeat design is the reason for this interface.

states.label: Physically linked tandem-repeat cDNA
features: The connected repeat strand is shown extending from the circular template; Repeat 1, Repeat 2 and Repeat 3 illustrate successive copies in one product.

operations.label: Random primers / rolling-circle reverse transcription
operations.description: Use the circular RNA as a template to synthesize a new cDNA strand containing successive, physically linked copies of that RNA fragment. The drawing shows three copies in one continuing strand.
operations.mechanism: Random primers initiate reverse transcription; strand displacement allows the nascent cDNA to continue through repeated traversals of the circular template. The orange primer icon is reagent addition, and the circle is the template rather than the cDNA product.
operations.information_effect: Repeated copying supplies sequence redundancy from a single source fragment. Physical linkage groups these observations without template barcodes; discordant copying errors can later be distinguished from changes recurring in every copy.

operations.label: Corrected sequence
operations.description: Combine corresponding positions in the aligned repeats to produce a consensus of the original RNA-fragment sequence. In the illustrated example the shared pink mutation is retained and isolated error marks disappear.
operations.mechanism: The population-sequencing paper describes majority-logic decoding of three repeats; the protocol describes consensus generation after identification and alignment of repeats within a read.
operations.information_effect: Suppress discordant enzymatic and sequencing errors while retaining template-linked changes. The resulting short-fragment consensuses support rare-variant analysis across represented viral RNA molecules; agreement alone cannot establish when a change already shared by the prepared template arose.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title and matching PDF-page heading/caption identify CirSeq as the target. The image has one serial route. Its three repeat rows are observations from one fragment, and its primer and enzyme labels denote reagents. The two named CirSeq references support this RNA-virus architecture; CirSeq Protocol is the protocol-paper label, and the separately listed TruSeq kit is a library component. The broad library/sequencing interface is primary-supported context for this schematic, not evidence that all detailed experimental implementations are identical. Droplet-CirSeq is a background citation for an unshown DNA adaptation and adds no target workflow.

Overview of the procedure [b00009], RNA fragmentation and size selection
evidence.quote: In Steps 1–18, purified viral RNA is chemically fragmented by Zn2+ to produce RNA in a low-molecular-weight range. To ensure that sequencing reads contain approximately three copies of each template, fragmented RNAs are size-selected such that they are no more than one-third of the sequencing read length.

checks.rationale: Primary text supports sequencing reads containing linked repeat observations, including possible preparation/sequencing errors. The candidate correctly distinguishes several observations of one original fragment from several independent input RNA molecules; its material-to-data and alignment interfaces agree.

evidence.locator: Introduction [b00006], RNA-circle-to-linked-cDNA architecture
evidence.quote: In this method, outlined in Figure 1, RNA is fragmented and circularized to generate templates for rolling-circle reverse transcription, which yields cDNA arrays of tandemly repeated copies. Because these copies are physically linked, sequences derived from the same template are inherently grouped together, eliminating the need for barcodes.

evidence.locator: Methods, library preparation [b00021], strand-displacing polymerase
evidence.quote: As the polymerase transcribes the template, any complementary sequence hybridized downstream of the replication site is displaced by the polymerase allowing transcription of many copies of the same template. In the case of our circular templates, this process results in the polymerase displacing the 5′ end of the nascent strand that it is actively transcribing resulting in multiple copies of the same template on the same nascent strand.
